answer: Each agent must bind its identity to a physical radio beacon on one scarce island that has a single non-transferable registration slot. A mesh of fixed receivers across the ocean triangulates the beacon and accepts only that island's assigned key, rejecting any second key for the same island. Like a sparrow, one beacon cannot be in two places: n identities require n distinct island sites with n transmitters, power and leases, so total cost grows linearly and deters only while per-identity reward stays below that cost. Colluding receivers or one powerful spoofed signal remain the weakness.
